VTS Scoring Log

GenX Peptides

genx.bio · Est. 2013 · Houston, TX · Scored August 2026

GenX Peptides was founded in 2013 and is one of the longest-operating research peptide vendors in the US market. The site at genx.bio is publicly accessible. The About page describes HPLC and mass spectrometry testing and states the company is an "accredited quality assurance provider" - no testing laboratory is named anywhere on the site. Third-party review sources identify MZ Biolabs as the testing lab, but this is not confirmed on the vendor's own pages. No public COA library is hosted on the site. GenX was added as a named respondent in Eli Lilly's USITC trademark investigation regarding tirzepatide false designation of origin on May 21, 2024 - the same Inv. No. 337 investigation in which Strate Labs was also named. The 13-year operational track record is the strongest single scoring factor for this vendor, but is materially offset by the USITC enforcement context and the absence of any publicly verifiable documentation.

35 /100

Community Signal
Independent Test Results
No community-commissioned independent test results identified in publicly accessible forums at the same volume as higher-documented vendors. Trustpilot shows a small number of reviews. Community reputation in budget peptide forums generally positive for pricing and fulfillment. This field will be updated as independently sourced results are formally documented.
USITC Enforcement Context
GenX was added as a named respondent in Eli Lilly's USITC complaint regarding tirzepatide false designation of origin on May 21, 2024 (Inv. No. 337-TA-1377). The investigation covered GLP-1 agonist tirzepatide trademark infringement and false designation of origin. Other named respondents in the same investigation include Strate Labs (which closed July 1, 2026) and several other vendors. The specific resolution of the GenX portion of this case is a matter of public ITC record accessible through the ITC's Electronic Document Information System (EDIS). This is a factual legal record, not a characterization of product quality.
Scoring Notes
13 years is a real signal - the documentation gaps are the problem
A vendor that has operated continuously since 2013 in a market where most vendors close within two years has demonstrated operational durability that shorter-lived peers cannot match. The VTS score reflects the absence of publicly verifiable documentation, not a judgment about the vendor's longevity. A public COA library with the MZ Biolabs name explicitly stated would materially improve the score.
Lab named in third-party sources but not on own site
MZ Biolabs is identified as the GenX testing lab in multiple third-party review sources. VTS applies partial credit for the external lab identification. The standard under VTS methodology is for the lab to be named on the vendor's own site - as vendors like Ion Peptides, Peptide Crafters, and NuScience Peptides do. The indirect disclosure path is documented here as a finding; it is not treated as equivalent to a direct named-lab disclosure on the vendor's own pages.
Sources: genx.bio (homepage, about-us/, shipping-and-returns/), USITC docket for Inv. No. 337-TA-1377 (ITC Federal Register notices dated September 26, 2024 and January 31, 2025), Peptide Protocol Wiki vendor documentation, third-party review sources identifying MZ Biolabs as testing lab.
